subject: Re: Immediate: FastRetail first-token latency surge / p95-p99 regression
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jmiles@fastretail.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: FastRetail Ops <ops@fastretail.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 15:42:00 +0000
Subject: First-token p99 spike hitting checkout — urgent

Hi Markus / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sudden regression in first-token latency for requests to the hosted API used by our checkout personalization service. p95 is up ~300ms and p99 is spiking >1.2s since ~14:30 UTC. This started right at the same time your hosted API release window ended — not sure if related.

Impact: checkout API timeouts for ~12% of requests (affecting cart conversions).

What I can share: attached are three representative traces and a screenshot of the dashboard. Trace IDs: fr-20270809-1a2b3c, fr-20270809-1a2b8f — they show large TLS handshake RTTs before first byte.

Can we get an immediate call and an ACK that you're investigating?

Thanks,
Jordan Miles
Sr. Platform Engineer, FastRetail
jmiles@fastretail.com

Attachments: fastretail_traces_20270809.txt, screenshot_latency_0809.png

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 15:55:00 +0000
Subject: Re: First-token p99 spike hitting checkout — urgent

Hi Jordan — thanks for the quick flag and the traces. We see the same signal in our telemetry (p95/p99 TTFT uptick starting ~14:25 UTC).

Immediate plan:
- I've looped in Monica (SRE) to triage network/TLS/CDN impact.
- Monica, can you correlate the customer trace IDs and confirm whether this is upstream (CDN) or our ingress?
- Evelyn / Sean: please stand by for possible routing fallback and an exec note.

We will share an initial update within 30 minutes and propose a mitigation (workaround) if we can. Apologies for the disruption — we understand checkout latency is critical.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Jordan Miles <jmiles@fastretail.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 16:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: First-token p99 spike hitting checkout — urgent

Thanks Markus / Jordan — initial findings from SRE triage:

What we see (summary):
- TTL: p99 TTFT for FastRetail traffic to hosted-us-east has increased starting 14:24 UTC.
- Trace correlation: the customer trace IDs show the majority of delay occurred during TLS handshake / TCP connect on the CDN edge hop (Avery edge cluster eu-west-2-similar-pop).
- Our ingress latencies to the origin/gateway remain nominal.
- Datadog: TLS handshake RTT distribution shows a bimodal shift in ~2 edge nodes (see attached histogram).

Immediate mitigations attempted:
- We pushed a short-lived routing rule to prefer alternate edge pops for FastRetail; saw a ~40% reduction in sampled p99 in the first 10 minutes.
- We added a temporary connection keepalive tweak for pooled upstream sockets.

Next steps (requested):
1) Ask Avery Solutions (CDN) to investigate handshake timeouts and TLS renegotiation stats for the affected edge cluster — forwarding their support contact now.
2) If Avery confirms edge degradation, we will coordinate an automated fallback to alternate pops for FastRetail until they remediate.
3) Prepare an RCA and propose a customer credit for the window.

Attachments: handshake_histogram_20270809.csv

— Monica Patel
SRE Lead, Redwood Infra
monica@redwood.com

Avery team — attaching sample customer traces and our handshake histograms. We observe elevated handshake RTT and some SYN-retry counts on edge cluster "eu-west-2-pop-14" for connections originating from our gateway to your edge. Please advise ASAP: is there any recent config rollout, cert rotation, or infra noise that could explain TLS handshake slowness?

Customer: FastRetail (FR-2381) — affected since ~14:25 UTC.

Requested: expedited investigation and recommended mitigation steps (routing rules, keepalive, HTTP/1.1 fallback, TLS config checks).

Attachments: fastretail_traces_20270809.txt, handshake_histogram_20270809.csv

— Monica

From: Avery Solutions Support <support@averycdn.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Jordan Miles <jmiles@fastretail.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: URGENT — possible TLS handshake regression impacting FastRetail (ticket 9876)

Hi Monica / Redwood team,

Thanks for the data. We've opened internal ticket 9876 and our edge ops are actively profiling the eu-west-2-pop-14 nodes. Preliminary check: a recent kernel upgrade on a small subset of edge nodes correlated with increased TCP SYN retries and sporadic TLS resumption failures; that is consistent with higher handshake latencies. We are:

- Rolling back the kernel change on affected nodes (ETA 45m).
- Suggest enabling keepalives and increasing the handshake timeout as an immediate mitigation.
- As a short-term workaround, we can provide a configuration to prefer alternate POPs for FastRetail.

We'll update this ticket with progress. Attaching the initial ticket PDF.

— Avery Solutions Support
support@averycdn.com

Attachments: support_ticket_9876.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jmiles@fastretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 16:33:00 +0000
Subject: Update: FastRetail TTFT regression — temporary mitigation applied / next steps

Jordan — update from our side:

- Root cause: initial SRE and vendor analysis points to upstream CDN edge node instability (kernel upgrade regression) causing elevated TLS handshake RTTs at the edge cluster serving some of FastRetail's traffic.
- Mitigation: Avery rolled back the change on the affected nodes and we applied an automatic POP-fallback policy for FastRetail during the window; sampled p99 TTFT improved ~60% in the affected slices.
- Customer impact window: ~14:25 UTC — 15:10 UTC on Aug 09 (we're still validating final tail improvement).

Next steps / commitments:
- We'll share an RCA draft by EOD tomorrow including detailed traces and timeline.
- If you'd like, we can schedule a post-incident review with Avery for next week.
- We're preparing a service credit proposal for the impact window; I'll follow up once we finalize numbers.

Sorry again for the disruption and thanks for working through this with us. If you want an immediate POA or a call to walk through the traces, happy to hop on.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com
